site: every portal (the agent's own history and answer bank)
class: A store that silently falls back to a second, smaller store, and a derived cache that is rebuilt from whichever store is open
symptom: Questions the agent had answered correctly before were asked again. Logs showed about 1,800 'Postgres unavailable -- using SQLite' lines (20-23 Oct). Postgres held 57 applications and 172 answers, SQLite 22 and 61, with only 4 applications in both; the answer bank held 9 entries where 35 were learnable.
root_cause: tracking.open_tracker fell back to SQLite whenever a configured Postgres was unreachable, so history was recorded in two databases; answer_bank.rebuild deleted and rebuilt the bank from whichever one was open, so a smaller store shrank it. It also learned the agent's answers only from sent applications, so answers on held applications were never reused.
why_tests_missed: The fall-back was a documented, intended behaviour with no test, and the bank was only ever built from one complete tracker in tests; nothing built it twice from trackers of different sizes.
fix: A configured Postgres that is down now raises an error naming 'docker compose up -d' (TRACKER=sqlite stays the explicit opt-out). answer_bank.rebuild merges into the existing bank (ranking you > confirmed > reviewed, then newest; forgotten keys stay out; kept entries must still pass portable()). Agent answers on needs_user_review and ready_to_submit applications are learned as 'reviewed'. Page copy and 'Not specified ...' answers are refused. The 18 SQLite-only applications and their rows were copied into Postgres once, additively, after a pg_dump.
prevention: Never let a store silently change under a run: fail loudly, and make any opt-out explicit. A cache derived from a store must be added to, not rebuilt from scratch, so a smaller source cannot destroy it; test it by building twice from sources of different sizes.
